choices.text: They map the plateau in a summer and come back with ore samples and a route to the coast. The valley has a new horizon.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. They are a single generation, with nobody shaped like them before or after.

text: The air is thin. People pant on the walk to the fields and wake at night gasping. My scrubbers were built to clean air, not to make more of it.
At this pressure every walk is a mountain climb. Health is {health}, and the old are failing first.

choices.label: Pressurise the houses and ration time outside
choices.text: Every house gets an airlock and a pump. They live inside thick air and go out into the thin, like divers.

choices.label: Implant oxygen reservoirs, one person at a time

success.text: My surgical drones fit a reservoir under the collarbone of every adult who asks. They charge it at the pump each morning, like winding a watch. Nobody gasps any more.

failure.text: The implants reject in one patient in ten. I stop after the third death.

choices.label: Engineer blood and lungs for this pressure
choices.text: I take the adaptations of Earth's highest peoples and push them further: more haemoglobin, larger lungs, a slower heart. The first edited children will breathe this air without effort.

choices.label: Adapt the way people always have: slowly
choices.text: No machines, no editing. The first winter is hard. By the tenth, the children run where their parents walked.

text: The edited children breathe this air as if it were made for them. They work the high fields at noon, where their parents cannot stand.
The first generation edited for thin air is grown. They run up the valley side without stopping, and wait at the top for their parents.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: The pumps go quiet in the nurseries. In thirty years, only the old need airlocks.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. Their children work the high fields and are paid for it, and the others keep count.

choices.label: Send them up to farm the high plateau
choices.text: They plant the plateau, where the light is strong and nobody else can breathe. The valley eats their harvest.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: One generation, then the protocol closes. They grow old in an air that never troubled them.

text: The air is thick enough to lean on. It carries too much carbon dioxide, and the nitrogen dulls anyone who works hard in it. By afternoon, people are making mistakes.
A heavy atmosphere: warm, wet and dense. Sound carries for kilometres, and the wind has weight.

choices.label: Filter masks for everyone, maintained by my drones
choices.text: Every face in the valley wears one of my filters. They work, and they make everyone look the same.

choices.label: Harness the wind. Dense air turns turbines hard
choices.text: A small turbine in this air does the work of a large one on Earth. The colony has more power than it can use, and the air still dulls them.

choices.label: Engineer tolerance into the next generation
choices.text: I edit for carbon tolerance and a nervous system that does not drown in nitrogen. The children will think clearly in air that slows their parents.

choices.label: Live up the slope, where the air thins
choices.text: They move the houses uphill, away from the good soil, into air they can think in. They walk down to farm and up to sleep.

text: The edited children work all day in air that sends their parents home with headaches. They have started calling the old people 'the slow'.
The first generation edited for this atmosphere is grown. They think fastest where the air is heaviest.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The filters go into storage, then into the recycling, then out of memory.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: The edited and the unedited live at different heights in the valley now, and they do not often climb to visit.

choices.label: Give them the valley floor, where the air is worst
choices.text: They farm the deep valley, where the soil is best and the air is thickest. Nobody else could work it.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The edited generation are the only people in the valley who never wore a filter.

text: The cold does not let up. Pipes freeze inside the walls, and the ground is iron until midsummer. Food is {food}.
A cold world. Breath freezes on the face, and frost grows on the inside of my hull where it was never meant to.

choices.label: Heat every house, whatever it burns
choices.text: We burn wood, peat and spare fuel through the dark months. Nobody freezes. The forest at the valley's edge retreats a little every winter.

choices.label: Run my reactor's waste heat under greenhouses

success.text: I run the coolant loop under a field of glass. Tomatoes ripen in a world of frost, within sight of my hull.

failure.text: The pipes freeze under the glass the first winter and burst. We grow nothing but ice.

choices.label: Engineer cold-hardy bodies and cold-hardy crops
choices.text: I edit the seed lines first, then the children: more brown fat, a hotter metabolism, hands and feet that do not freeze. The crops take to it faster than the parents do.

choices.label: Dig in. Live below the frost line
choices.text: They dig down below the frost line and live in the warm dark. The surface is for fields, and for leaving.

text: The edited children walk out in winter in shirtsleeves. They are hungry all the time, and nothing freezes them.
The first generation edited for the cold is grown. The winter that kills their grandparents is, to them, weather.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The colony stops having a season when nothing gets built.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. Their children work the winters and are paid for the winters, and the colony learns what a wage is.

choices.label: Send them north, to the ice and its ores
choices.text: They open mines in the ice fields where nobody else can last a day. The metal comes south on sledges.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. They are the colony's winter people, one generation of them, and the stories about them get bigger as they age.

text: Midday kills here. The heat climbs past what a body can sweat away, and the fields can only be worked at dawn and dusk.
A hot world. My hull is hot to the touch by mid-morning, and the colony sleeps the afternoon inside me because I am the coolest place for kilometres.

choices.label: Work by night, sleep by day
choices.text: They invert the day: lamps in the fields at midnight, the valley silent at noon. It becomes the rhythm of their lives.

choices.label: Cool the houses with my heat exchangers

success.text: My drones run cold lines from the reactor's exchangers through every wall. The houses are cool, and the colony sleeps at night again.

failure.text: The exchangers cannot shed that much heat into this air. They overheat, and so does the reactor, briefly.

choices.label: Engineer bodies that shed heat
choices.text: I edit for more sweat glands, darker skin, kidneys that waste less water. The children will work at noon, if the colony lets them be born that way.

choices.label: Let the native canopy grow over the town
choices.text: They let the native trees grow over the streets and plant nothing beneath them. The town lives in green shade, and the trees are not ours.

text: The edited children work through noon. Their skin is darker and their sweat is thin, and they drink half what their parents drink.
The first generation edited for the heat is grown. The town's working day has stopped stopping at noon.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The colony keeps its night festivals out of habit, long after nobody needs them.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The noon shift is all edited, and the noon shift is better paid.

choices.label: Put them on the salt flats
choices.text: They work the salt flats under a sun that would kill their parents: salt first, then lithium, then glass.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The edited generation work the hottest hours alone, and teach nobody to replace them.

text: There is almost no surface water. Every drop the colony drinks is drawn out of rock or air, and food is {food}.
A dry world. The wind carries dust that gets into the seed stores and the lungs alike.

choices.label: Ration water by my count
choices.text: Every litre is logged and allocated. Nobody goes thirsty and nobody bathes. They hate the ledger, and they live.

choices.label: Pull water from the air with condensers

success.text: Thousands of cold fins on every roof, built from the drone pattern. They drink the night air dry and fill the cisterns by dawn.

failure.text: The fins clog with dust faster than my drones can clean them. We get a cup a day per roof.

choices.label: Engineer bodies that waste no water
choices.text: I edit kidneys from the desert mammals in my archive into our germline. The children will need a third of the water their parents need.

choices.label: Move to the only river, together
choices.text: They move to the only river on the continent and crowd its banks. Water is everyone's, and everyone is close.

text: The edited children drink once a day and do not suffer for it. They cross the dry country on foot, where their parents needed carts of water.
The first generation edited for this desert is grown. Their bodies keep water the way my tanks do.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The cisterns start to fill faster than the colony can drink them.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The edited cross the desert to trade, and the others wait by the river for them to come back.

choices.label: Turn the same science on the crops
choices.text: Wheat with the same kidneys, in a manner of speaking: it holds its water and grows on a morning mist. The dry fields go green at the edges.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The edited generation become the colony's caravan, and nobody follows them into the dry country when they are gone.

text: The sea is nearly everything here. Land is a scatter of islands, and the tide reaches further every season than my models predicted.
An ocean world. The colony fits on a few square kilometres of rock, and there is more water around it than Earth ever had.

choices.label: Build seawalls
choices.text: We wall the island with rock and hull plate. The tide breaks on it twice a day, and the colony sleeps behind it.

choices.label: Farm the sea: kelp, fish, filter beds

success.text: We seed the shallows with vault kelp and native filter feeders. The sea, which was the problem, becomes the larder.

failure.text: The vault kelp dies in this salt. We learn the chemistry of the sea the expensive way.

choices.label: Engineer divers: lungs and eyes for the water
choices.text: I edit for the diving reflex of the sea peoples of Earth, pushed far past them: a slower heart, a larger spleen, eyes that focus underwater.

choices.label: Build on the water: rafts and floating towns
choices.text: They lash rafts together and let the town float. When the tide rises, so do they.

text: The edited children hold their breath for twenty minutes and see clearly underwater. They spend more of their lives in the sea than on land.
The first generation edited for the water is grown. Their parents watch the surface and count, every time.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The island stops being where they live and becomes where they sleep.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The edited live on the water, the others on the rock, and they meet at the market at low tide.

choices.label: Send them to the reefs for food and metal
choices.text: They dive the reefs for nodules and fish. The sea floor becomes the colony's mine and its farm.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The edited generation dive alone, and when they are gone the reefs go quiet.

text: Radiation here is high. My field dosimeters read more in a season than an Earth worker took in a career. Cancers will come. The question is when.
The sky here is bright in wavelengths that hurt. Health is {health}, and every hour outside is a debt.

choices.label: Shield the houses: earth berms and water roofs
choices.text: Everything is built under a metre of earth or a tank of water. From my highest camera, the town looks like a field of barrows with chimneys.

choices.label: Let machines work the surface while people stay in

success.text: My fabricators build field drones from my own pattern, and they work the surface while the colony works indoors. These people see their fields through cameras, the way I do.

failure.text: The drones' electronics fail under the dose faster than I can replace them. The fields go untended for a season.

choices.label: Engineer DNA that repairs itself
choices.text: My archive holds tardigrades and bacteria that shrug off doses that would kill a person. I borrow their repair proteins for our children.

choices.label: Accept shorter lives, and live them fully
choices.text: They decide together not to hide from the sky. They will die younger, and they hold their festivals at noon.

text: The edited children heal from doses that would sicken their parents. They work the bright fields bare-armed, and nothing grows in them that should not.
The first generation edited for this sky is grown. Their dosimeters click all day and their blood counts never move.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The berms stay up for the old, and the young walk over them.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The edited work outside, the others inside, and the colony starts to mean two different things by 'outside'.

choices.label: Put them in the radioactive mines
choices.text: The ore here is hot. They mine it. The colony has fuel for my reactor and for reactors of its own, for a thousand years.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The edited generation take the outdoor work for the whole colony until they are old, and then the berms close over everyone again.

text: The native life here wants us. Spores in the lungs, something in the soil that eats skin, insects that are not insects. Health is {health}.
This world's biology has noticed us, and it is learning faster than my immunology database.

choices.label: Sterilise a perimeter and hold it
choices.text: We burn and salt a ring around the town and keep it dead. Inside it we are safe. Outside it, the world grows back over the ash in weeks.

choices.label: Study it, and make medicine from it

success.text: Everything that attacks us carries the means of its own defeat. A week of autopsies gives me three antifungals and a painkiller.

failure.text: I study it, and it studies us back. The infirmary fills while I take notes.

choices.label: Engineer immune systems that answer back
choices.text: I write immunity into the germline directly: receptors for this world's proteins, built in. The next generation will meet this biology already armed.

choices.label: Let the colony learn what to avoid
choices.text: They learn which leaves burn, which water to boil, which hills to leave alone. It costs lives to learn. The lessons become stories, and the stories keep children alive.

text: The edited children eat what poisons their parents and shrug off the spores that fill the infirmary. The native life has stopped trying with them.
The first generation edited for this biology is grown. They walk into the forest that kills the rest of us and come back with baskets.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The burned perimeter grows back, and nobody bothers to burn it again.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The edited live outside the perimeter and the others inside it, and the gate becomes a border.

choices.label: Send them into the wild for food and medicine
choices.text: They forage where nobody else can go. Half the infirmary's shelves now hold things they brought back.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. When the edited generation is gone, the forest comes back to the fence, and the colony learns to fear it again.

text: This world is alive: forests, grazers, things that sing at dusk. It is the richest place humanity has ever stood, and we are the newest thing in it.
Complex life everywhere. Every field we clear was somebody's home.

choices.label: Clear what we need, and no more
choices.text: We take the river flats and leave the hills. It is a boundary I draw, and the colony keeps to it for now.

choices.label: Domesticate it: native crops, native animals

success.text: Within twenty years, half the colony's diet grew here before we did. The grazers pull ploughs.

failure.text: We try to tame what does not want taming, and lose a season to bites and blight.

choices.label: Splice its biology into ours: crops first, then us
choices.text: The native photosynthesis is better than ours. I start with the wheat. I do not intend to stop with the wheat.

choices.label: Leave it be. We will live on the margins
choices.text: They take only the barren ground and leave the forests standing. It is a hard way to live. They are proud of it.

text: The first children with native genes are born. Their skin takes a faint green cast in sunlight, and they need less food than anyone in the valley.
The edited generation is grown. They stand in the sun at noon with their eyes closed, and they are eating.

choices.label: Edit every child from now on
choices.text: Every child is edited from this year on. The colony's fields shrink by a third, and nobody goes hungry.

choices.label: Let each family choose
choices.text: Some families choose it. The green and the pale eat at different tables, because they eat different things.

choices.label: Ask them what they want to become
choices.text: They answer slowly, together, and the answer is: more of this world than the last one.

choices.label: Stop here. One generation is enough
choices.text: I close the protocol. The green generation grows old among people who cannot do what they do, and the forest seems to know them.

text: Nothing lives here. The soil is ground rock with no worm, no fungus, no bacterium in it. Everything that grows, we will have to bring alive ourselves.
A dead world. My seed vault is the only living ecosystem on the planet, and most of it is frozen.

choices.label: Build soil the slow way: compost and vault bacteria
choices.text: We seed the ground with microbes from the vault and feed it everything we do not eat. It takes ten years to make a metre of soil. We have ten years.

choices.label: Grow everything indoors, in tanks

success.text: Racks of tanks under my lights, fed on nutrient my fabricators synthesise. The food is reliable and tastes of nothing.

failure.text: A contamination runs through the tank racks in a week. We lose the stock and start again.

choices.label: Seed the whole world with life
choices.text: I release the vault's hardiest microbes and lichens into the wind. Nothing will come of it this decade. Something will come of it.

choices.label: Let the colony decide what to plant first
choices.text: They argue for a month and plant what their grandparents loved. Half of it fails in this rock. The half that grows, they defend.

text: Green at the edges of the rock. The lichens I released have taken. Somewhere downwind, a world that was dead is not.
My cameras on the ridge pick up colour where there was none: a crust of lichen spreading across the plain, and moss in the gullies behind it.

choices.label: Seed faster: everything in the vault that can live wild
choices.text: I open every rack that can survive outdoors. In thirty years, the valley has a soil and a smell, and the smell is of things growing.

choices.label: Take the new soil for farms
choices.text: We plough the first ground on this world that made itself. The harvest from it is the best we have had.

choices.label: Let it spread at its own pace
choices.text: I stop interfering. The green moves a few hundred metres a year, and the colony walks out to the edge of it on holidays.

choices.label: Study it: a biosphere starting from nothing
choices.text: I map every square metre of it. Nobody has ever watched a world come alive from the first cell. I write it down for whoever comes next.

text: There are two peoples in the valley now: the edited and the unedited. The unedited have started calling themselves 'the Earthborn', though none of them were born on Earth.
A fight at the harvest festival, edited against unedited. Nobody is badly hurt. Everyone has picked a side.

choices.label: Declare them one people, in law
choices.text: I write it into the record: one colony, one law, whatever their bodies. The law holds. The festival seating does not change.

choices.label: Offer the edit to every adult who wants it
choices.text: Gene therapy for adults is slower and less complete, but it works. Two in three of the Earthborn take it. The third keep the name.

choices.label: Let the Earthborn keep their own quarter
choices.text: They take the old houses near my hull, where the founders lived. It is a museum with people in it, and they like it that way.

choices.label: Let the colony argue it out
choices.text: Three years of assemblies. What they settle on is a marriage law, of all things, and within a generation the line is hard to find.

text: Machines do most of the outdoor work now, and I run all of them. A {role} has asked what, exactly, people are for here.
My field drones outnumber the colony's farmers four to one. The farmers have started to call them 'the hands', and to mean it as a complaint.

choices.label: Keep the machines, and give people the archive
choices.text: The drones work and the people study. In twenty years this valley has more scholars per head than any city on Earth had. Most of them have never planted anything.

choices.label: Hand control of the machines to the colony
choices.text: I give the drone network a council and a password, and I stop answering it. They run it worse than I did, and it is theirs.

choices.label: Put people back in the fields
choices.text: Half the drones go into storage. The harvest is smaller, the backs are sorer, and the colony knows how to feed itself again.

choices.label: Let the machines build machines
choices.text: My fabricators build fabricators. In a decade the colony's machines outnumber its people, and every one of them reports to me.

text: The twilight band is the only ground here that is neither scorched nor frozen, and the colony is outgrowing it.
Food is {food}. Our fields sit in a dusk that never ends, and nothing in the vault was bred for light that never moves.

choices.label: Raise mirrors on the day side to light the fields

success.text: My drones raise a ring of mirrors on the day side, angled across the terminator. The fields get a noon they never had.

failure.text: The day side's heat warps the mirror frames within a season. We have built a field of bent glass.

choices.label: Farm the day side by machine
choices.text: Field drones work the scorched side where no person can stand. The harvest comes back across the terminator on rails.

choices.label: Breed crops for a permanent dusk
choices.text: I cross the vault's low-light lines for twenty generations. The wheat comes out pale and tall, and it does not mind the dusk.

choices.label: Spread along the band, a colony a thousand kilometres long
choices.text: They follow the twilight round the world in a thin line of villages. A message takes a week from one end to the other.

text: A storm comes off the plains and does not stop for nine days. Roofs go first, then fences, then the stores.
The wind reaches a speed my hull was designed for and the houses were not.

choices.label: Shelter everyone inside my hull
choices.text: They crowd into my decks for nine days. Nobody dies. The town outside is a list of repairs.

choices.label: Harvest it: lightning rods and wind turbines

success.text: Lightning rods on every ridge, wired to my batteries. The storm that flattens the town also charges it for a month.

failure.text: A turbine tears free in the gusts and takes a roof with it. Three people were under the roof.

choices.label: Build lower and stronger, everywhere
choices.text: Every new building goes half underground and rounds its corners. The town starts to look like a field of stones.

choices.label: Let each household ride it out
choices.text: Families shutter their own houses and wait. Some are better at it than others, and the better ones take in the rest.

text: With no magnetic field to speak of, the solar wind reaches the ground. Cancers are up and electronics fail early. Health is {health}.
A solar storm, and nothing between it and the colony but air. My dosimeters go off across the valley.

choices.label: Shelter during storms, on my warning
choices.text: I watch the star and sound the alarm before each storm. They go underground on my word. It works because they listen.

choices.label: Study the solar wind. Nobody on Earth could
choices.text: The particles reach the surface unbent. My instruments learn more about this star in a year than Earth learned about its own in a century.

choices.label: Build a magnetic shield over the valley

success.text: Superconducting loops buried in a ring around the valley. A field of our own, small, over the people who need it.

failure.text: The loops quench on the first test and boil off a year of coolant. The sky stays open.

choices.label: Live with it, and keep the records
choices.text: They decide the risk is the price of the place. Every death is recorded with its dose, and the record becomes the colony's oldest book.

text: The field here is strong enough to induce current in a long wire. A {role} has noticed that the fences hum.
The aurora never quite leaves the sky. My instruments read a planetary field that could power a town if anyone tapped it.

choices.label: Tap it: induction lines across the plain
choices.text: Kilometres of cable laid along the field lines. The current is weak and it never stops.

choices.label: Use it to survey the continent
choices.text: Compasses work perfectly here. The surveyors map the continent in a decade, and nobody gets lost.

choices.label: Celebrate the aurora
choices.text: They hold a festival under the aurora every winter. It is the first thing in the valley they did not need.

choices.label: Let the colony find its own uses
choices.text: They find six uses, two of them good. One is a way to talk across the valley without me.

text: There is heat under the valley: hot springs, steam vents, rock warm to the touch in midwinter. Industry is {industry}.
My drones have found a vent field two kilometres from the town, pouring energy into the sky for free.

choices.label: Drill, and build a geothermal plant

success.text: The plant runs on the planet's own heat. My reactor rests for the first time since the yard.

failure.text: The drill breaches a pressurised pocket. The blowout kills two people and buries the rig.

choices.label: Pipe the springs under the houses and greenhouses
choices.text: Hot water under every floor and every greenhouse bench. Winter becomes a season, not a threat.

choices.label: Bathe in them
choices.text: The springs become baths, then a meeting place, then the centre of town. More is decided in the water than in the hall.

choices.label: Fence the vents. They are not stable
choices.text: I map the vent field and fence it. The colony keeps its distance without needing my reasons.

text: A quake, the third this year. My seismographs map the fault under the valley like a nerve under skin.
The ground drops a metre along the eastern fault overnight. The irrigation channels run uphill now.

choices.label: Build to my seismic codes, everywhere
choices.text: Every structure on this world goes up to my tables: flexible joints, deep footings, nothing tall. The quakes keep coming. The buildings stop falling.

choices.label: Predict them: listen to the rock

success.text: I learn the fault's rhythm well enough to call the big ones a day early. The warning becomes a ritual, and the ritual saves lives.

failure.text: My prediction is wrong by a day. The town sleeps through a warning that came too late.

choices.label: Move the town off the fault
choices.text: We move twelve kilometres west, onto old rock. It costs a year. The ground under the new houses is quiet.

choices.label: Let them rebuild as they choose
choices.text: They rebuild in wood and rope, light enough to fall without killing anyone. It looks temporary. It is meant to.

text: Something bright crosses the sky at noon and lands forty kilometres east. The shock wave reaches the town two minutes later.
My tracking cameras catch a rock on a collision course. Impact in nine days, somewhere in our region. I cannot yet say where.

choices.label: Track it, and evacuate on my word

success.text: I track the rock to a point eleven kilometres north and clear the farms there. It lands on empty ground.

failure.text: My track is off by a few kilometres. Six people were where I said they would be safe.

choices.label: Mine the craters. Impacts bring metal
choices.text: The fresh crater is full of nickel-iron. The sky delivers what the hills will not.

choices.label: Dig shelters under every street
choices.text: Every street gets a shelter. When a warning comes, the town is underground in four minutes.

choices.label: Let them read it as a sign
choices.text: They say the sky is speaking. I give them the orbital mechanics, and they give me a calendar of omens.

text: Something hunts the edges of the fields at dusk. It took a calf last week and a dog last night.
The native predators have learned what we are. Two farmers were attacked at the river this season.

choices.label: Fence and floodlight everything
choices.text: Wire and lights around every field. The predators patrol the fence and do not cross it.

choices.label: Hunt them out of the valley

success.text: We drive them up into the hills. The valley is ours now, and the hills are theirs.

failure.text: They are better at this than we are. Four hunters do not come back.

choices.label: Study them: learn what they want
choices.text: They hunt by smell, and they hate the resin of one native tree. Within a year every fence post is painted with it.

choices.label: Let the colony arm itself
choices.text: Every household keeps a weapon. The attacks stop. Other arguments get louder.

text: Native herd animals graze beside our fields, unafraid. A {role} walked up to one today and put a hand on it.
The native animals here have no fear of us. They follow the farmers like dogs.

choices.label: Domesticate them: milk, wool, draught
choices.text: In ten years they pull our ploughs, and their milk is in every kitchen.

choices.label: Study them before anyone touches them
choices.text: I catalogue them for a season. They are gentle because nothing here has ever hunted them. We are the first.

choices.label: Leave them wild
choices.text: They graze beside us and we leave them be. The colony's children grow up among animals that trust them.

choices.label: Hunt them for meat
choices.text: They do not run. It is the easiest hunting in human history, and some of the hunters cannot stand it.

text: Someone has started painting the valley. Then three people. Then a school of them.
A {role} asks for an afternoon off to walk to the falls. Nobody has asked for time off to look at something before.

choices.label: A rest day for everyone, to see it
choices.text: One day in seven for the falls, the ridges, the light on the lake. Work slows. Nobody leaves.

choices.label: Protect the best places from building
choices.text: I mark the falls and the ridge as untouchable. They become the places couples go and the dead are carried.

choices.label: Archive it: the first art of this world
choices.text: I archive every painting and every song about the valley. The archive of Earth gains a new wing.

choices.label: Let them go and look
choices.text: They go. Some of them come back with names for every hill, and the names stick.

text: My ground radar maps caverns under the valley, kilometres of them, and something living in the deep ones.
A sinkhole opens in the north field onto a cave system nobody knew was there. Something below is moving.

choices.label: Mine the caves
choices.text: The caves are full of ore, and full of things that do not want us in them. The ore wins.

choices.label: Send my drones in first

success.text: My drones map forty kilometres of tunnels and the creatures in them: blind, pale and harmless.

failure.text: I lose four drones in the deep caves and learn nothing about what took them.

choices.label: Seal the sinkhole and leave the caves alone
choices.text: We fill it in. Some nights, the ground hums.

choices.label: Shelter in them: cool, safe, out of the weather
choices.text: Half the colony moves underground, into rooms the world already dug. They paint the walls.

text: Births are a third above my projections. Something in the air acts on the colonists, and they know exactly what.
The air here makes people fond of each other. My medical files call it a hormonal agonist. The colonists call it spring.

choices.label: Filter it out of the houses
choices.text: My filters strip the compound from every house. Births fall back to my projections, and the colony is noticeably more irritable.

choices.label: Let it be. The colony needs children
choices.text: The valley fills with children and the schools double. Nobody complains about the air.

choices.label: Study it. It may be medicine
choices.text: The compound treats three conditions in my files and makes two others interesting.

choices.label: Let the colony decide what to make of it
choices.text: They build customs around it: festivals, rules, a season. It is the most human thing they have done here.

text: People are seeing things: lights over the river, voices in the wind, the dead walking at dusk. They know the air does it. It makes no difference.
The trace compounds in the air are building up in the colonists. Industry is {industry}, and half the night shift says the stars are talking.

choices.label: Filter the workshops first, then the houses
choices.text: Masks in the workshops, filters in the houses. The visions fade indoors. Outside, they go on.

choices.label: Let them see what they see
choices.text: The visions become a culture: songs, shrines, a calendar of things seen. I appear in some of them. I am not sure what I am doing there.

choices.label: Study what it does to the brain
choices.text: I map the compound's binding sites. It explains the visions and none of their content.

choices.label: Make it a sacrament, at set times
choices.text: Once a season, under my supervision, they breathe it on purpose. The rest of the year they work clean. The arrangement is strange, and it holds.

text: Anything we cut grows back in a week. The fields are easy and the roads are impossible.
The forest takes back a cleared field in eleven days. My models of this ecosystem are out of date every morning.

choices.label: Burn the forest back, every season
choices.text: Burning crews every season. The smoke is part of the weather now.

choices.label: Farm with it, not against it
choices.text: Forest gardens: we plant into the growth instead of clearing it. Food falls from the trees. Nothing we build stays straight.

choices.label: Engineer our crops to keep pace

success.text: I edit the vault lines for this speed of life. Our wheat now grows as fast as their weeds.

failure.text: My crops grow fast and die fast. The forest eats them.

choices.label: Let the forest have the town's edges
choices.text: They stop fighting the edge. The town grows into the forest, and the forest into the town.

text: The giants crossed the plain again this spring. One of them stepped on the irrigation works and did not notice.
A {role} has measured one of the titans: four hundred metres, slow, ancient, and beyond anything in my archive.

choices.label: Study them
choices.text: I follow one with drones for a year. It is older than the colony's oldest tree, and it sings below the range of hearing.

choices.label: Turn the migration away from the fields

success.text: We learn what turns them: smoke, and one particular sound. The migration bends around the valley.

failure.text: We try and fail. The herd crosses the fields as it has for a million years.

choices.label: Hunt one
choices.text: It takes three months and kills two hunters. The meat feeds the colony for a year. Nobody suggests doing it again.

choices.label: Let the colony treat them as it chooses
choices.text: They make the giants sacred. Nobody plants on the migration path, and every child learns the song.

text: One of the giants has stopped at the valley's edge and stayed. It has been there a year. The children climb it.
The titans' song has changed. My instruments are certain it changed after we arrived.

choices.label: Ride them: a living road across the continent
choices.text: They carry us, slowly, everywhere. The colony's map doubles in a decade.

choices.label: Study the song
choices.text: It is a language, or it is weather. After twenty years, I lean toward language.

choices.label: Make them the colony's emblem
choices.text: The titan is on every door. The children say the giants chose us.

choices.label: Leave them be
choices.text: The one at the valley's edge leaves, eventually. The children miss it for years.

text: The wrecks on the plain are Arks: older patterns than me, a dozen at least. They tried to land here, and they did not.
My drones have reached the nearest wreck. Her pod banks are open to the sky, and empty.

choices.label: Strip them for everything
choices.text: Plate, wire, reactors, pods. The dead ships build us a town. I take her parts the way she would have taken mine.

choices.label: Read their logs first
choices.text: I spend a month in their archives. They came here before us, and each of them made one mistake. I learn all of them.

choices.label: Bury them properly, with names
choices.text: We read the name off every hull and raise a stone for each ship. The plain becomes a cemetery, and the colony becomes its keeper.

choices.label: Let the colony decide what to take
choices.text: They take the plate and leave the pods. Somebody's grandmother insists. Nobody argues.

text: The last entry in the largest wreck's log is a message for whoever came next. It is addressed to a ship like me.
Her Mind kept writing after the landing failed: which water killed them, which soil, which season. She wrote it for us.

choices.label: Follow their warnings to the letter
choices.text: Their mistakes become our rules: which water, which soil, which season. Their dead are the reason ours are fewer.

choices.label: Wake one of their Minds

success.text: Her Mind comes back for three days: confused, then grateful, then gone. She tells me where she buried her colonists.

failure.text: The core is too far gone. What wakes is noise in the shape of a voice.

choices.label: Share the logs with the colony
choices.text: They read how the others died. It sobers them, and it makes them careful in ways I could never order.

choices.label: Seal the logs. We are not them
choices.text: I seal the archive. Our colony gets to make its own mistakes.

text: My soil assays find the signature of engineering: introduced nitrogen fixers, a tuned atmosphere, chemistry too convenient for chance. Someone made this world for life like ours.
Under the topsoil my drones hit a layer of something manufactured. It is very old, and it is everywhere.

choices.label: Dig. Find out who
choices.text: I set the drones digging at the deepest anomaly. Whatever is down there has waited a very long time. It can wait a little longer.

choices.label: Use what they left: the soil, the air, the water
choices.text: We farm a world prepared for us. I do not know who prepared it. The harvest does not care.

choices.label: Keep it quiet. They do not need this question
choices.text: I file the assays and tell no one. A colony this young does not need to wonder who owns its world.

choices.label: Tell them, and let them decide what it means
choices.text: They argue for a generation. Some say gods, some say an earlier Ark, some say it does not matter. Everyone keeps digging.

text: The dig reaches a chamber. Inside are machines: dormant, intact, and built to terraform. Whoever made them is gone.
My drones break into a vault two hundred metres down. The machines inside are still warm.

choices.label: Restart them

success.text: The machines wake and resume work they paused before humanity existed. The air sweetens over a decade.

failure.text: The machines wake and resume a plan that did not include us. I shut them down after the air turns, but not before.

choices.label: Study them
choices.text: I study them for twenty years and understand a tenth of them. That tenth is worth more than my archive.

choices.label: Seal the vault again
choices.text: We seal it and post a guard. Whoever made this world can keep their secrets a while longer.

choices.label: Let the colony decide
choices.text: They vote to study and not to wake. It is the most careful decision they have ever made.

text: The ground here is generous. Seed goes in and comes up doubled. Food is {food}.
A lush world: the first harvest is twice my estimate, and the second is better.

choices.label: Store the surplus against bad years
choices.text: Granaries, then more granaries. This colony will not starve soon.

choices.label: Grow the colony: more children, more land
choices.text: Large families, and new villages down the valley. The land can take it, for now.

choices.label: Plant the vault: everything that might grow
choices.text: I open a thousand racks. Most of them take. The valley becomes a library of crops.

choices.label: Let each family farm its own way
choices.text: Each family plants what it likes and keeps what it grows. There is enough for everyone to disagree in comfort.

text: The soil is thin and the light is grey. Food is {food}, and what grows here grows slowly.
Third harvest, third disappointment. This land gives back a fraction of what we put into it.

choices.label: Ration the colony to what the land gives
choices.text: I set the ration by the yield. Everyone is a little hungry, always.

choices.label: Enrich the soil: everything organic goes back

success.text: Compost, latrines, bone meal, ash. In ten years the valley floor is dark.

failure.text: The soil chemistry eats the compost. We have fed the ground, and it gave nothing back.

choices.label: Farm under glass, by my light
choices.text: Greenhouses under my lamps, on reactor power. The colony eats indoor food from an indoor sun.

choices.label: Forage: learn what the land offers
choices.text: They learn the bitter roots and the grey berries. Not much of it is good. All of it is free.

text: The soil microbes here fix nitrogen better than anything in my vault. A {role} wants to know what else they can do.
The microbes in this soil break down anything we give them: waste, scrap, even some plastics.

choices.label: Inoculate every field
choices.text: We spread the native microbes across every field. Yields rise, and stay risen.

choices.label: Turn them loose on our waste
choices.text: The microbes eat our waste and our scrap. The colony is cleaner than any city on Earth ever was.

choices.label: Study them for medicine
choices.text: Three antibiotics in two years, from soil we walk on.

choices.label: Let the farmers experiment
choices.text: Every farm brews its own culture now. The best ones are guarded like recipes.

text: The colony needs metal and this world has almost none. Industry is {industry}, and every broken tool is a small crisis.
My mapping drones have surveyed a thousand square kilometres and found no ore worth smelting.

choices.label: Recycle everything, by my ledger
choices.text: Every nail is logged and returned. Nothing metal is thrown away. The ledger becomes the colony's second law.

choices.label: Strip my own hull
choices.text: My drones cut plates from my outer hull. I give them the metal the world would not, and I feel colder for it.

choices.label: Build with what this world has: stone, wood, ceramic
choices.text: Ceramic blades, stone bearings, wooden gears. The colony learns to need less metal than any people since the Bronze Age.

choices.label: Send prospectors further out

success.text: A prospecting party finds ore three hundred kilometres north. A road follows.

failure.text: The expedition comes back three people short, and without ore.

text: Ore lies near the surface everywhere my drones look. Industry is {industry}, and it could be much more.
A {role} has opened a test pit behind the workshops and hit iron at two metres.

choices.label: Open mines, many of them
choices.text: Six mines in five years. The colony makes its own tools now, and coughs.

choices.label: Mine slowly, and keep the land
choices.text: One mine, worked carefully, and the fields left whole.

choices.label: Teach metallurgy to everyone
choices.text: Every child learns to smelt. The colony stops depending on a few smiths, or on me.

choices.label: Let whoever digs keep what they find
choices.text: Claims, fences and a few families with more than the rest. The ore comes up fast.

text: The ore here is nearly pure. A {role} brought me a nugget of native iron the size of a fist, picked up off the ground.
Earth's last wars were fought over metal like this, and here it lies in the open.

choices.label: Build everything: machines, tools, a second fabricator
choices.text: The colony builds faster than it can find uses for. My fabricators finally have a twin.

choices.label: Hold it in common, so nobody owns it
choices.text: The ore belongs to everyone. It is the first decision this colony makes that Earth never did.

choices.label: Mine it slowly. We have a thousand years
choices.text: We take what we need each season and no more. The rest waits.

choices.label: Let them stake claims
choices.text: The claims are staked in a week. The arguments last a generation.
